Verified Sapient mainnet receipt: view evidence ↗

Save the exact report bytes, then optionally anchor their SHA-256 digest on our deployed mainnet contract. View contract publication ↗

Local export only. No fees or wallet approval required.

Request recovery details are stored in this browser. Approval and submission are separate steps.

Use the developer wallet instead

After exporting your report, download a manifest and load it in the Manifest page of your mainnet developer wallet. It creates the same receipt and reads all getters. The wallet uses public fees from your default account. Estimate the fee and review it before submitting. After clicking Submit once, open Transactions to check the result; the wallet can return to the same form without a success message. Do not click Submit again.

    1 / 4Prepare your test wallet

    02 / TRY IT YOURSELF

    One experiment. One step at a time.

    We’ll guide you through two tiny test payments to yourself, then compare the visible account references.

    User-operated · Testnet only
    1. Public fee

    A private self-payment, with fees taken from revealed funds.

    2. Private fee

    The same requested payment, with fees taken from a stealth output.

    3. Compare & test

    Inspect explicit account references and run a local regression mutation.

    Start by connecting your wallet using the top-right control. No test transaction has been requested.

    Account & funding requirements

    You need revealed test TARI for the first fee, plus shielded test TARI for both payments and a separate private fee input. Specter does not request private-balance access or automatically shield funds.

    STEP A

    Self-payment with public fee

    Creates an enforced transparent-fee request in Sapient. Review it there; it is not submitted automatically.

    Not started

    STEP B

    Self-payment with private fee

    The same recipient, resource, amount and fee cap. The enforced fee funding mode changes to private.

    Not started

    The assertion covers explicit declared inputs and direct component call targets. It does not prove anonymity. Equal hidden payment terms come from the requests, not independent public proof. Timing, public fees, signatures and graph links may still expose information.
